quiz.correctFb: Section 43 establishes civil liability and monetary damages payable to victims for unauthorized system access and contamination. When acts in Section 43 are committed dishonestly or fraudulently, they become criminal offenses under Section 66, carrying up to 3 years imprisonment.
distractors: The IT Act covers all computer systems, networks, and electronic devices universally.
Section 43 is a civil remedy with no prison sentence; Section 66 carries up to 3 years imprisonment.
Section 66A was struck down in Shreya Singhal (2015); Section 43 and Section 66 remain fully active laws.

quiz.q: Under Section 66F of the Information Technology Act 2000, what is the maximum punishment prescribed for the offense of Cyber Terrorism against the sovereignty and integrity of India?
opts: A monetary fine of ₹50,000 only
Imprisonment for life
Community service for six months
Rigorous imprisonment up to one year
quiz.correctFb: Section 66F of the IT Act penalizes Cyber Terrorism—acts that threaten the unity, integrity, security, or sovereignty of India or strike terror in people by denying access to computer resources. It carries a statutory penalty of imprisonment for life.
distractors: Cyber terrorism is a severe national security felony and cannot be compounded with a simple fine.
Community service is not a statutory sentencing disposition under the IT Act.
One year is far below the statutory life imprisonment penalty mandated by Section 66F.

quiz.q: Under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act 1872, what is legally required for electronic records (such as printouts, server logs, or emails) to be admissible as secondary evidence in a court of law?
opts: The hard drives must be physically melted in court
A signed Certificate of Authenticity executed by a person occupying a responsible official position in relation to the relevant computer device
A verbal testimony from any internet service provider employee
Electronic records are strictly inadmissible in Indian courts under all circumstances
quiz.correctFb: Under Section 65B(4), secondary electronic evidence is legally inadmissible unless accompanied by a written certificate signed by a person occupying a responsible official position, certifying that the computer was operating properly and that the data is authentic.
distractors: Physical destruction of evidence is a criminal offense (destruction of evidence) under Section 204 IPC.
Verbal oral testimony cannot substitute for a mandatory written Section 65B certificate.
Electronic records are fully admissible under Indian law provided the procedural mandates of Section 65B are satisfied.

quiz.q: According to the Order of Volatility in digital evidence acquisition (RFC 3227), which of the following evidence sources must be collected first before powering off a machine?
opts: Hard disk optical storage drives
Registers and CPU cache, followed by main system memory (RAM)
Archival tape backups stored offsite
Printed network architecture diagrams
quiz.correctFb: The Order of Volatility dictates that the most ephemeral, volatile data must be captured first: CPU registers and cache, followed by routing tables, ARP cache, and main system memory (RAM), before non-volatile hard disks.
distractors: Hard disk magnetic/optical storage is non-volatile and persists after power-down.
Archival backup tapes are long-term non-volatile storage and can be examined days later.
Paper diagrams are static physical documents with zero digital volatility.

quiz.q: Why is a Bit-Stream Disk Image (physical sector-by-sector clone) required in digital forensics rather than a standard logical file copy (like drag-and-drop)?
opts: A bit-stream image takes 10 times less hard drive space
A bit-stream image captures all unallocated space, slack space, and deleted file fragments that are ignored by a logical copy
A logical copy automatically encrypts all files with military-grade AES-256
Bit-stream copying is only possible on mobile phones, not on desktop computers
quiz.correctFb: A bit-stream disk image copies every physical sector sequentially, including unallocated space, slack space, and swap files where deleted evidence and hidden data reside. A logical copy only copies currently visible active files.
distractors: A bit-stream image is equal in size to the entire capacity of the source physical disk.
Logical copies do not perform encryption; they simply copy files using the OS file manager.
Bit-stream imaging is standard across hard drives, SSDs, USB drives, servers, and mobile devices.

quiz.q: Under the Cloud Security Shared Responsibility Model, which party is primarily responsible for securing the physical servers, datacenter facilities, and virtualization hypervisor in an IaaS environment?
opts: The enterprise customer's internal desktop support team
The Cloud Service Provider (e.g., AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud)
The regional telecom fiber optic contractor
The end-user accessing the web application from an iPhone
quiz.correctFb: In the Shared Responsibility Model, the Cloud Service Provider (CSP) is exclusively responsible for 'Security OF the Cloud'—encompassing physical datacenter security, power, heating, physical servers, and the virtualization hypervisor.
distractors: The customer's internal team manages guest operating systems and application configurations, not physical datacenters.
Telecom carriers provide transit bandwidth, not cloud virtualization security.
End-users manage their personal client devices, not cloud server infrastructure.

quiz.q: What primary attack vector did the Mirai botnet exploit to compromise and enslave hundreds of thousands of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in 2016?
opts: Advanced quantum cryptanalysis breaking 4096-bit RSA keys
Automated scanning for open Telnet ports paired with a dictionary of 61 default factory-shipped credentials
Physical micro-probing of silicon chips in electronic factories
Exploiting buffer overflows in quantum satellites
quiz.correctFb: The Mirai botnet scanned the public internet for open Telnet and SSH management ports on IoT devices (cameras, DVRs, routers) and brute-forced them using a hardcoded list of just 61 factory default username/password pairs.
distractors: Mirai utilized trivial unauthenticated credential brute-forcing, not quantum cryptanalysis.
Mirai operated purely over IP networks without physical chip tampering.
Satellites were not involved; consumer IoT cameras and home routers were the primary targets.

quiz.q: Under the 2022 cybersecurity directions issued by CERT-In under Section 70B of the IT Act, what is the mandatory timeframe for organizations to report specified cybersecurity incidents?
opts: Within 30 calendar days
Within 6 hours of noticing the incident
Within 72 hours of incident resolution
Annually during the company's financial audit
quiz.correctFb: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) directions mandate that all service providers, intermediaries, data centers, and corporate bodies must report specified cybersecurity incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of notice.
distractors: 30 days is common for long-term audit reports, but violates incident disclosure rules.
72 hours is the European Union GDPR personal data breach reporting timeline, not Indian CERT-In.
Annual reporting applies to financial taxes, not active cybersecurity incident mitigation.

quiz.q: What is the primary operational objective of the 'Lessons Learned' phase in the NIST SP 800-61 Incident Response Lifecycle?
opts: To publicly identify and fire the system administrator responsible for the initial vulnerability
To evaluate how effectively the response team handled the incident, identify operational gaps, and update security controls to prevent recurrence
To calculate the total monetary ransom to pay to the attackers
To permanently disable all network monitoring tools to reduce logging costs
quiz.correctFb: The Post-Incident Activity (Lessons Learned) phase conducts a blameless post-mortem analysis to evaluate what occurred, why it occurred, how well the team responded, and what defensive controls and playbooks must be updated to prevent recurrence.
distractors: Blameless post-mortems focus on process, architectural, and systemic improvement rather than punitive action.
Incident response frameworks strictly emphasize containment and recovery rather than paying extortion.
Disabling monitoring directly contradicts the objective of strengthening detection capabilities.

bossChallenges.scenario: A financial institution in Assam experiences a severe cyber incident: an external hacker penetrates internal networks, alters client account balances, and exfiltrates confidential transactional databases to a server in Europe. Law enforcement and the digital forensics team are summoned. Structure an exhaustive investigation and legal report: map out the digital forensic investigation lifecycle (preservation with write-blockers, bit-stream imaging, hash verification), formulate the Chain of Custody requirements and Section 65B certification under the Indian Evidence Act, and identify all applicable penal sections under the Information Technology Act 2000 (Sections 43, 66, 66C, 66F, and 75).
rubric: Digital Forensics Acquisition Rigor (2.5 marks): Complete procedural description of live RAM capture, hardware write-blocker usage, bit-stream disk imaging (dd/E01), and MD5/SHA-256 integrity verification.
Chain of Custody & Evidence Admissibility (2.5 marks): Comprehensive documentation of evidence handling logs and full legal compliance with Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act.

Statutory Mapping under IT Act 2000 (2.5 marks): Accurate legal application of Section 43 (civil damages), Section 66 (hacking), Section 66C (identity theft), Section 66F (cyber terrorism if critical financial infrastructure is compromised), and Section 75 (extraterritorial jurisdiction).
Forensic Pitfalls & Anti-Forensics Countermeasures (2.5 marks): Critical analysis of anti-forensic techniques (timestomping, disk wiping) and how to avoid evidence contamination during triage.

bossChallenges.scenario: A healthcare cloud provider hosting electronic medical records across an IaaS environment suffers an unauthorized data exfiltration event. The board of directors is confused regarding legal liability, incident reporting deadlines, and cloud responsibilities. Clarify the Cloud Security Shared Responsibility Model for IaaS, and provide a compliance roadmap specifying the mandatory CERT-In 6-hour incident notification protocol and NIST containment phases.
rubric: Cloud Shared Responsibility Demarcation (1.25 marks): Explicitly defining the boundary between the CSP's physical/hypervisor duties and the customer's OS/data/IAM responsibilities.
Regulatory Notification under CERT-In (1.25 marks): Detailing the mandatory 6-hour reporting window under Section 70B of the IT Act 2000.
Incident Containment & Evidence Triage (1.25 marks): Formulating rapid network micro-segmentation and forensic memory capture without disrupting active life-safety clinical monitors.
Root Cause Remediation & Governance (1.25 marks): Conducting a post-incident lessons learned review and implementing multi-factor authentication and data encryption at rest.
